title: The decision's holdout interval measured on a time split: time_decision_v1
request: The owner, 2026-10-25: measure the time-split interval after tonight's gate (34.1's open end: a time split passes no folds, so its interval is the row-sized one, never measured; the churn replica's first day-by-day reading realised 10.6 against an interval of 4.8 to 8.6).
spec: dclab_rnd/time_decision_measure.py, campaign time_decision_v1: 30 fresh seeds (100 to 129) of the churn replica, split by time, each run twice through the engine: a share capacity read as one pool and one call a day read day by day; fraud_decision_v3's gate per arm (coverage of at least 80% of at least 20 acting seeds, centre, width) plus a time-split check and one holdout read; the next step fixed with the gate; per run the positive rates of the out-of-fold rows, the latest fold and the holdout, and each fold's value.
plan: Copy fraud_decision_v3's campaign shape and gate
Two arms per seed on the same replica
Review the design before the gate freezes
Commit the code, then run from a clean worktree at that commit
Report each arm's verdict and act on the next step fixed with the gate

decisions.decision: Two arms on the same seeds: a share (pooled) and one call a day (day by day)
decisions.why: the share tests the time split's interval itself, the daily arm tests 0.115.0's day-by-day reading on the same rows, so a difference between them belongs to the days

decisions.decision: The gate copied from fraud_decision_v3, judged per arm
decisions.why: the same yardstick that passed on an entity split, so a failure here belongs to the time split

decisions.decision: Record positive rates and each fold's value, never a row value
decisions.why: the review: a realised value above the interval has two possible causes on this replica (its planted drift and the expanding-window fold models' weakness); the counts let the report say which

decisions.decision: dclab-core 0.118.0: on a time split the holdout-sized samples come from the latest fold's rows (sample_rows); the expected value's interval still reads every row
decisions.why: v1's pre-registered next step: the latest fold is the period nearest the holdout

decisions.decision: v2 keeps the all-folds interval on the same seed beside the measured one, reported, never gated
decisions.why: the review: drawing from a third of the rows also widens the interval by about 1.22 times, so a pass could come from width, not a better centre

decisions.decision: dclab-core 0.118.1: the holdout's drift note when the interval comes from the latest rows, shown in the solution report
decisions.why: v2's pre-registered step for a centre still above 0: say the drift past the training period, which no interval from past rows holds

findings.defect: the split was recorded as None on every run
findings.scenario: a probe of run_one on seed 0: neither final['run'] nor final['evidence'] holds the split
findings.cause: the strategy lives in the data stage's evidence (split_strategy)
findings.fix: read it from the data stage, and a time_split gate so a seed split otherwise never counts toward a time-split verdict

findings.defect: the next step named a cause the campaign could not tell from another
findings.scenario: the churn replica drifts on purpose (later sign-ups leave more: out-of-fold positive rate 0.217, latest fold 0.236, holdout 0.246 over seeds 100-129), so realised above centre is expected from the drift alone; seed 0's probe missed above on both arms
findings.cause: the next step was written as 'the fold models weaker than the final one'
findings.fix: the next step worded as a remedy (read the interval from the latest fold's rows), and each record keeps the three positive rates and each fold's value

findings.defect: the replica's planted traps never labelled the runs' decisions
findings.scenario: fraud_decision_v3 calls labels.from_replica; this campaign dropped it, losing 60 runs' benchmark labels

findings.defect: a run that raised left no record, so the campaign could never reach a verdict
findings.scenario: one seed raising keeps 'complete' false forever, and fixing it changes the code hash the frozen campaign refuses
findings.fix: a failed result is written; the chosen gate counts it

findings.defect: a second run after completion crashed on the verdict file
findings.scenario: the glob TDC-[0-9]*.json matched TDC-900_decision.json, which has no seed
findings.cause: a glob wider than the runs' names

findings.defect: v2's step for a centre below 0 named a cause that moves width, not the centre
findings.scenario: had v2 ended with mean z -0.5, the step 'sample the latest two folds' would have widened the interval and lowered its centre: the wrong cause treated
findings.cause: too few rows widen an interval; they do not push its centre one way
findings.fix: centre below 0 keeps 'correct the optimism of choosing the model'; 'sample the latest two folds' moved to the too-wide branch

findings.defect: v2 could pass from a wider interval and say a better centre, and its 'above 0' step named only drift
findings.scenario: from v1's numbers the pooled mean z would move from 0.80 to about 0.32 against a bound of 0.30, about 0.07 of it from widening alone
findings.cause: the latest fold is a third of the out-of-fold rows; and its model is still fitted on fewer rows than the final one
findings.fix: each run keeps the all-folds interval on the same rows and seed, with its z, reported beside the gate; the 'above 0' step names drift or the fold model's fewer rows

findings.defect: no test held the engine to the latest fold, nor the entity path
findings.scenario: writing '== 0' for the last fold's number would have passed every test; the entity branch of sample_rows never ran
findings.cause: tests checked the method's words only
findings.fix: the campaign test checks the flagged rows are the last 600 out-of-fold rows (TimeSeriesSplit(3) of 2,400); a core test with entities checks the interval moves up and says whole entities

findings.defect: a bootstrap draw with none of the near rows fell back to every row, mixing two intervals
findings.scenario: one near entity of 3 rows: about 37% of draws used every row and the rest repeated that entity, giving [-1.0, 7.2] against [5.4, 7.8]
findings.cause: the empty-pool fallback took the whole draw
findings.fix: such a draw samples the near rows or entities themselves; the engine reads every fold, with a note, when the latest fold holds fewer than 20 rows or entities

findings.defect: an insert placed the paired reading inside an if branch
findings.scenario: a text replacement keyed on '    within = None' matched the indented line inside 'if acted is None:', breaking the if/elif
findings.cause: a replacement anchor that is a substring of a deeper line
findings.fix: read the lines and put the block before the if

measurements.name: time_decision_v1: 30 fresh seeds of the churn replica (split by time), two arms, on 17cfbd36
measurements.gate: time_decision_gate_v1 per arm: chosen, time split, capacity and one holdout read, coverage of at least 80% of at least 20 acting seeds, |mean z| <= 1.645/sqrt(N), the 90% chi-squared interval of RMS z contains 1

Positive rate out-of-fold 0.217, latest fold 0.236, holdout 0.247; each fold's value (pooled share) 4.81, 5.19, 5.59 against 5.96 realised

the per-fold values are read at the chosen share pooled, for both arms

measurements.name: time_decision_v2: the latest fold's interval (dclab-core 0.118.0) on 30 fresh seeds (130 to 159) of the churn replica, on 71c4c617
measurements.result: pooled (10% share): pass on every gate; 28 of 30 inside (2 above), mean z 0.12 (bound 0.30), RMS z 0.98 (0.81 to 1.25). daily (one call a day): fail on the centre only; 26 of 30 inside (4 above), mean z 0.40, RMS z 1.12 (0.92 to 1.42). Paired all-folds interval on the same seeds: mean z 0.84 and 1.29, 24 and 19 of 30 inside. The latest fold's interval is 1.21 and 1.17 times wider. Positive rate out of fold 0.217, latest fold 0.237, holdout 0.253; the latest fold is the last 600 out-of-fold rows on every run
limits: the daily arm still fails its centre: drift past the training period
one drifting replica; a table without drift is not measured

outcome: On a time split the decision's interval now comes from the latest fold: with a share capacity it passes every gate on a drifting replica (mean z 0.12, from 0.84 on the same seeds), and with one call a day it improves (1.29 to 0.40) but stays above, the drift past the training period being said beside the reading.
lessons: Before a measurement names a cause in its next step, check whether the test data plants another cause with the same sign
A campaign must write a record for a run that fails, or a frozen campaign can never reach its verdict
An interval built from the past is for a world that stays the same: on a drifting table it says so by missing on one side
When a fix also widens an interval, keep the old interval on the same seeds: the paired reading tells a better centre from a wider one
risks: The churn replica's drift and the fold models' weakness push the same way; the rates separate them only roughly
